key_insight: SparseDecoding improves LLM decoding by pruning with calibration data collected from autoregressive generation, so the pruning objective matches the token distribution seen at inference.
engineering_relevance: By aligning pruning and adding a decoding-optimized sparse SpMV kernel, the method targets the actual memory bottleneck in LLM inference and delivers real wall-clock speedups.
method: Build layer-wise calibration matrices from dense-model autoregressive activations, excluding prefill.
Prune with a Hessian-guided objective matched to decoding-time activations instead of fixed natural-text calibration.
Use an optimized N:M SpMV kernel with bitmask indexing and fixed-step traversal for efficient sparse decoding.
evidence_signal: On Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.3-70B, and Qwen3-14B/32B, the method outperforms standard fixed-text calibration on long-form generation and reaches up to 1.48x end-to-end decoding speedup on A100 GPUs.
watch_item: The speedup depends on sparse-kernel support and hardware efficiency, so benefits may vary with sparsity pattern, model architecture, and GPU implementation details.
paper_title: SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference
